modern: You will soon die, and you are not yet simple, nor free from disturbance, nor free from suspicion of being hurt by external things, nor kindly disposed towards all; nor do you yet place wisdom only in acting justly.
original: Thou wilt soon die, and thou art not yet simple, nor free from perturbations, nor without suspicion of being hurt by external things, nor kindly disposed towards all; nor dost thou yet place wisdom only in acting justly.
notification: You will soon die, and you are not yet simple, nor free from disturbance, nor free from suspicion of being hurt by external things, nor kindly disposed towards all…
notification_original: Thou wilt soon die, and thou art not yet simple, nor free from perturbations, nor without suspicion of being hurt by external things, nor kindly disposed towards all…

explained.summary: You’ll be dead soon, Marcus tells himself, and you still aren’t simple, still get rattled, still suspect that outside things can hurt you, still aren’t kind to everyone, and still don’t see that wisdom lies only in acting justly. It’s an honest self-reproach. He’s measuring himself against his own ideals and finding the gap, with time running out.
